newsitem.title: BELGIUM: MOURY CONSTRUCT TO FLOAT ON BRUSSELS BOURSE.
newsitem.headline: MOURY CONSTRUCT TO FLOAT ON BRUSSELS BOURSE.

text.p: The family dominated Moury construction company said on Thursday it would float shares in its newly formed building group, Moury Construct, on the Brussels Forward Market on December 20.
The company stems from the absorption of Moury and Bemat by Solinvest on November 18 1996. At the same time Solinvest was renamed Moury Construct.
This IPO is the last phase of a complex process aimed at streamlining Moury, Bemat and Solinvest into one single new company.
The company said it would offer 112,500 new VVPR shares at 3,000 Belgian francs per share. As a result the total number of shares will increase from 289,452 to 401,952 shares.
The subscription period will start on December 2 and end December 13, 1996. Bemat and Solinvest will be removed from the first and the second markets respectively.
The restructuring of the Moury group is aimed at simplifying its various operations and making its shares more attractive on the bourse.

"We want to simplify the structure of the company because in the past the family structure was too erratic and we want to achieve greater liquidity," Moury Construct's administrator J.P. Feldbush told Reuters.
The Moury family said they would retain 60 percent of Moury Construct while 40 percent would be offered to the public.

Managing director of Moury Construction Georges Moury said that the company's priority after floatation was to acquire or form a partnership with a construction firm in Flanders. He declined to give further details.
Moury's market capitalisation is 1.2 billion francs.

Moury Construct's 1995 operating income amounted to 1.8 billion francs, making it the 12th largest construction company in Belgium, according to Bank Degroof. It forecast operating income would rise to 1.95 billion francs for 1996.
Moury Construct has the bulk of of its activities in the Walloon provinces of Belgium and Brussels.

"The only drawback (for Moury Construct) is the group's high exposure to the poorly performing Walloon economy. Management is aware of this weakness and has clearly indicated external growth in Flanders is high on the strategic priority list," the Bank said.

Moury specialises in non-residential construction of industrial and office buildings, hospitals, sport centres and renovation. But it is also present in residential areas, particularly in social sector building.

Bank Degroof said the company's operating margins attained 8.1 percent on average over the past three years, compared to a sector average of 2.5 percent. The bank added that this was due to the management's continuous focus on the risk profile of its operations and a highly competitive cost structure.
"The various units now joined under the name Moury Construct will retain their identity and their individual skills," said Georges Moury.

Minority shareholders of Bemat (who in total hold 14,124 Bemat shares) will receive eight new Moury Construct shares in exchange of three Bemat shares. This public exchange operation will take place simultaneously with the IPO of Moury Construct between December 2 and December 13, 1996.
The minority shareholders of Solinvest and Bemat participating at the public exchange offering will have a priority right to subscribe to the new VVPR shares.
